This original synthetic article demonstrates explicit mathematical declarations,
an assumption, two associated proofs and a static glossary. The declarations
are in the local literal-JSON `knowledge.json` catalogue. They do not establish independent
mathematical review or formal verification.

::: {#def-square name="Square of a real number" am-macro="amSquare" am-args="value" am-intent="square($value)" am-tex="(#1)^2"}
The [square]{#concept-square} of a real number $x$ is the product $x\cdot x$,
written $x^2$.
:::

::: {#thm-square name="Positive squares"}
For every nonzero real number $x$, the square $x^2$ is positive.
:::

The term is defined in @def-square. [Read the assumptions](#assumption-real),
[follow the proof by signs](#prf-sign), or
[follow the proof using absolute value](#prf-absolute) for @thm-square.

::: {#assumption-real .am-assumption am-summary="Assumption: a nonzero real input"}
The input $x$ belongs to the ordered field of real numbers and satisfies $x\ne0$.
The nonzero condition excludes the case $x^2=0$.
:::

::: {#prf-sign .proof am-summary="Proof by signs"}
If $x>0$, the product $x\cdot x$ is positive. If $x<0$, then $-x>0$,
so $x^2=(-x)\cdot(-x)>0$. A nonzero real number has one of these two signs.
:::

::: {#prf-absolute .proof am-summary="Proof using absolute value"}
For a nonzero real number $x$, its absolute value satisfies $|x|>0$.
The product of two positive real numbers is positive, so $|x|^2>0$.
Since $|x|^2=x^2$, the conclusion follows.
:::
